clue.text: Doggy paddling often, of course, helps beginners

indicators.note: the beginners of the five words that follow are their opening letters, read in order

explanation.surface: Swimmers who start out are often helped by learning the doggy paddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginners' takes the first letters of 'paddling often of course helps'. 'Doggy' looks like part of the swimming stroke but is a noun here, a pet dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A doggy is a child's or informal word for a dog, as is the slang word for a pet hound.

clue.text: Cross put by number of promising clue

definitions.meaning: a cross written beside a number, as in plus five, marks it as above zero
a hopeful indication or encouraging sign

explanation.walkthrough: The plus sign is literally a cross, and it is also the sign used for numbers above zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus symbol marks a number above zero, and figuratively a hopeful indication is encouraging.

clue.text: Language once heard in huge prison

parts.note: OS is outsize, the clothing abbreviation for very large
the can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: An extinct tongue was once spoken in a vast jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' belongs to the definition: a language once spoken. Oscan was an ancient language of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscan is an extinct Italic language of ancient southern Italy, spoken in former times.

clue.text: Makes bequests extremely easily

definitions.meaning: passing possessions on to heirs, as in handing them down
winning with no effort at all

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads as the verb phrase with 'hands' as a verb; the second is the idiom for an easy win.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand things down is to bequeath them; winning without effort is winning by an idiomatic easy margin.

clue.text: Execute hellish plot

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld, so something of hell gives this name
a plot of ground is a patch

explanation.surface: Someone carries out a wicked scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: DIS is the classical name for the underworld (and its god), a common crossword stand-in for hell.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch someone is to kill them, the same as to execute them.

clue.text: Point duty

definitions.meaning: a single item or particular in an account
a small group or task assigned, as a military assignment

explanation.walkthrough: Point duty is a policeman's job directing traffic, so the clue reads as one phrase; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail is a particular item, and in military use a detail is an assigned task.

clue.text: A fitting device to make output of last worker yield more

definitions.text: A fitting device to make output of last worker yield more

parts.words: A fitting device to make output of last worker yield more
parts.note: a cobbler shapes footwear on a last, and this implement eases the foot into such footwear

explanation.surface: A gadget helps a cobbler's products stretch further.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is a cobbler's wooden foot mould, so the 'last worker' is a shoemaker; 'fitting' means putting on, not suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved implement slipped into the heel of footwear helps the foot go in easily.

clue.text: Emphatically anything that in New York could be X-rated

definitions.meaning: anything whatever, an old emphatic word for any amount at all

definitions.text: that in New York could be X-rated
definitions.meaning: in American usage the same word means zero, a nil score

explanation.walkthrough: Aught means anything at all; Americans also use it for nought, as in 'the aughts', so it is a nothing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Aught is an archaic word for anything at all, and in US English also a zero.

clue.text: Reduce punishment, accepting appeal, but leave no room for error

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the appeal goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: to reduce is to cut
a fine is a monetary punishment
it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A judge reduces a sentence after hearing an appeal but allows no mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeal' here is the slang 'it' for sex appeal, not a legal appeal against the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut it fine is to leave almost no margin of time or space.

clue.text: Good hunch tests out revised opinion

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A good hunch, once tested, leads to a revised opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the fourteen letters of GOOD HUNCH TESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Second thoughts are a reconsidered view reached after thinking again.

clue.text: Reveal what one might do with spill

definitions.text: what one might do with spill
definitions.meaning: a spill is a thin taper, carried to a flame to ignite it

explanation.walkthrough: A spill is a sliver of wood or paper for lighting fires, not something spilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something to light is to expose it; a taper is brought to a flame to be lit.

clue.text: I produce strains? Then I must get treated

indicators.note: letters that are treated are processed into a new form, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone straining with effort says they must get medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get treated' rearranges THEN I MUST. 'strains' suggests injury but means tunes or melodies.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer of popular songs produces melodies, which are strains of music.

clue.text: What a terrorist has hidden one found in vegetable basket

indicators.note: the words 'What a terrorist' contain the answer concealed across them

explanation.surface: A terrorist has hidden something in a basket of vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has hidden' points to letters running through whaT A TERrorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Tater is informal for potato, an item typically kept among vegetables.

clue.text: Half the capital provided for just one of these films

definitions.text: Half the capital provided for just one of these films

parts.words: Half the capital provided for just one of these films
parts.note: the second half of the Uruguayan capital's name spells one such film, so the answer is several of them

explanation.surface: Half the city's funds went on a single film.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital is MONTEVIDEO; its latter half gives one film, and the clue asks for the plural, so 'capital' is a city, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded films for home viewing are known by this name, the plural of a single recording.

clue.text: What was Hardy into? Could be at novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Was Hardy writing a novel, could it be?
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges COULD BE AT. Hardy suggests Thomas Hardy the novelist, but he is Oliver Hardy of Laurel and Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurel and Hardy were a classic comic pairing, a partnership of two performers.

clue.text: Resistance and rebel leader in novels

indicators.note: in places the rebel's leader inside the word for novels

parts.note: novels are works of fiction

indicators.note: the leader of the word rebel is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Resistance fighters and their rebel leader appear in novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives R from 'rebel', and 'in' puts it inside FICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction is the resistance one surface meets moving over another, or conflict between people.

clue.text: Labour loves to go into matter investigated in US jail

indicators.note: to go into means the first pieces sit inside the case

parts.note: a case is a matter under investigation
Lab is the abbreviation for Britain's Labour Party
love is zero in tennis, and O is zero, so loves give two Os

explanation.surface: A Labour scandal under investigation lands someone in an American jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loves' are tennis scores of zero, each read as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Calaboose is US slang for a local lockup or prison.

clue.text: In summer a gala wanting fine start

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: a gala is a festival

indicators.note: the start of the word fine is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A summer gala goes ahead without a good start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' is the opening letter of that word only, taken out of the gala word; AESTIVAL is the British spelling of estival.
explanation.definitionFit: Aestival describes things belonging to or occurring in the summer season.

clue.text: Force king to capture knight and lose recklessly

indicators.note: capturing means taking a piece inside, so the knight goes within the force and king

parts.note: a force, as in police force, can be a squad
N is the chess notation for a knight
ER is Edward Rex, a king

explanation.surface: A chess player forces the king to take a knight and recklessly loses.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess surface makes 'king' and 'knight' look like pieces being captured on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: To squander money or chances is to waste them recklessly.

clue.text: Quick to provide cover for Black Prince

indicators.note: providing cover means wrapping round, so alert surrounds black

parts.note: quick-witted means alert
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone quickly shields the Black Prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to provide cover for' puts B inside ALERT. The Black Prince is a famous English heir, but here 'Black' only gives B.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert, consort of Queen Victoria, is the best-known royal of this name.

clue.text: Religious reformer and rising painter, one often up on a charge

definitions.text: one often up on a charge

parts.note: Jan Huss was the Bohemian church reformer

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the word is read upwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A reformer and an ambitious artist are often charged with offences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns RA into AR. 'up on a charge' sounds criminal but means mounted for a cavalry charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a light cavalryman, a soldier who rides into a charge on horseback.

clue.text: Keep quiet about extremely unsuccessful prison system

indicators.note: about means around, so the gag goes round the extremes

parts.note: to gag someone is to keep them quiet

indicators.note: extremely takes the extremes of the word unsuccessful, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An official hushes up the failings of a prison system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' works on 'unsuccessful' only, taking its outermost letters rather than meaning 'very'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulag was the Soviet network of forced-labour camps, an entire penal system.

clue.text: Grunts at doctor's gadget

parts.note: grunts is US slang for infantry soldiers, GIs
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: Patients grunt at the doctor's equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grunts' looks like noises but means foot soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A gismo is an informal word for a gadget or device.

clue.text: After hitch, detect computer image

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first in the answer

parts.note: to thumb a lift is to hitch-hike
to nail a culprit is to catch or detect them

explanation.surface: After a snag, someone tracks down a picture on a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hitch' looks like a snag but means hitch-hike, as in thumbing a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail is a small preview version of an image on a screen.

clue.text: A university concealing decline for so long

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the decline sits within the other pieces

parts.note: to decline can mean to die away

explanation.surface: A university hides its decline for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' puts DIE between A and U. 'so long' looks like duration but is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for farewell, the same as the casual goodbye phrase.

clue.text: Success I have curing problem with breathing?

parts.note: a pass is success in an exam
I have contracts to I've
curing fish or meat can be done by smoking it

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a cure for their breathing problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curing' looks like healing but means preserving food by smoke. The question mark marks a definition by example: inhaling others' smoke harms breathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhaling other people's cigarette smoke is a hazard to lungs, so a respiratory problem.

clue.text: Pushchair's seen way before wave's given

indicators.note: before means the street piece comes ahead of the wave

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a roller is a long wave breaking on a shore

explanation.surface: A pushchair is seen on the road before a wave rolls in.
explanation.walkthrough: STROLLER is the usual American word for a pushchair.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroller is the American name for a baby's pushchair.

clue.text: With 100% backing it's time to be active

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for 100% is read in reverse

parts.note: something one hundred per cent is pure

explanation.surface: With full support, it is time to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns PURE into ERUP, then T is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano erupts when it becomes active, so to erupt is to burst into activity.
